core_obligations: Apply the algebra lemma to obtain the short exact sequence of multiplication by $s$ and the flatness of the quotient over $R$ (proof lines 1837-1840).
Deduce that each $s \in \Sigma$ acts as a universally injective $R$-module map $N \to N$ (proof lines 1840-1842).
Conclude that the localization map $N \to \Sigma^{-1}N$ is $R$-universally injective as the directed colimit of these maps (proof lines 1843-1844).
proof_roadmap: Exactness and flatness of the quotient (proof lines 1837-1840).
Universal injectivity of the homotheties (proof lines 1840-1842).
Universal injectivity of the localization as a colimit (proof lines 1843-1844).
difficulty_reason: The lemma refines the homothety situation over a local base: under the local homomorphism, finite presentation and flatness hypotheses, every element of the multiplicative set acts universally injectively and so does the localization map (statement lines 1820-1834, tag 05DF). The proof extracts a short exact sequence with flat quotient from an algebra lemma, converts flatness into universal injectivity, and passes to the directed colimit. The transport from flatness to universal injectivity is the substance, so the claim is H2.
